title: Shannon v. Shannon, S-25-546 (Neb. 2026)

reading.body:
This is a data ingestion failure rather than a deployment failure. The record was created from a source file that carried only the technical scaffolding of a document, its metadata, font settings and encoded layout data, and no article body. Whatever the underlying case may be, the incident entry holds no facts about it, so nothing about the system's behaviour in the world can be described from this record.

The failure sits at the point where a document is captured and parsed, before any summarisation or analysis step. A pipeline that treats a file's presence as evidence of readable content will pass an empty document downstream and produce an entry that looks like a catalogued incident while containing none of the substance. Catching it would have required a check on the extracted text itself, such as a minimum content threshold or a validation that the parsed body is non-empty, rather than a check that the file was retrieved successfully.

Nothing here establishes what Shannon v. Shannon concerns, what any court decided, or whether an AI system was involved at all. The two reports are court and legal database listings, and a filing or a published opinion is not a finding about any technology.

summary: The article text is a PDF file and contains no readable news content, so there is nothing to summarize. It consists only of technical metadata, font settings, and encoded data from an InDesign document, with no article body, facts, parties, numbers, or next steps. No summary can be produced from this file.
